overview.overviewText: This chapter explores Escape Velocity, Motion of A Satellite, Orbital Velocity, Time Period and Energy, providing comprehensive conceptual analysis, mathematical relationships, and structured applications grounded in NCERT authority.

blocks.title: 1. Key Academic Principles: Escape Velocity, Motion of A Satellite, Orbital Velocity, Time Period and Energy
blocks.contentMarkdown: Escape speed from Earth surface is the minimum projection speed to escape gravitational pull: v_e = sqrt(2 * G * M_e / R_e) = sqrt(2 * g * R_e). The numerical value of escape speed from Earth's surface is approximately 11.2 km/s and is independent of projectile mass and projection angle. The orbital speed of a satellite orbiting Earth at radius r is v_o = sqrt(G * M_e / r).

blocks.title: 2. Key Academic Principles: Escape Velocity, Motion of A Satellite, Orbital Velocity, Time Period and Energy
blocks.contentMarkdown: For a satellite in close Earth orbit, orbital speed is v_o = sqrt(g * R_e) ~= 7.92 km/s, and v_e = sqrt(2) * v_o. The orbital time period of a satellite is T = 2*pi * sqrt(r^3 / (G * M_e)). The total mechanical energy of an orbiting satellite is negative: E = - (1/2) * G * M_e * m / r, proving it is in a bound orbit.

blocks.title: 3. Key Academic Principles: Escape Velocity, Motion of A Satellite, Orbital Velocity, Time Period and Energy
blocks.contentMarkdown: Orbital Velocity of Satellite (v_o) in circular orbit at radius r = R_e + h: Centripetal force is provided by gravity: m * v_o^2 / r = G * M_e * m / r^2, so v_o = sqrt(G * M_e / r) = sqrt(g * R_e^2 / (R_e + h)). For Earth (M = 5.97 x 10^24 kg, R = 6.4 x 10^6 m): v_e = sqrt(2 * 9.8 * 6.4 x 10^6) ~= 11.2 km/s.
